_comment: Raspberry Pi Imager custom OS list for Sambuca.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS INSTEAD OF A FLASHER.
Sambuca previously shipped its own image writer: device enumeration,
raw device access, volume locking, elevation, download, checksum
verification, readback verification and a progress display. That was 855
lines reimplementing, badly and on one platform, what Raspberry Pi Imager
already does correctly on three. It took five attempts to get a single
Windows raw write working, which is the evidence that this code should
rpi-imager reads a custom OS list with --repo <url>. So Sambuca publishes
a list and launches the real tool. The user gets a mature, translated,
accessible GUI that handles UAC properly, and Sambuca keeps only the part
that is genuinely its own: what goes onto the card afterwards.
extract_sha256 and extract_size are the UNCOMPRESSED image, measured
locally on 2026-08-20 by decompressing and hashing the verified download.

os_list.name: Sambuca — Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit)
os_list.description: Raspberry Pi OS Lite, arm64. Sambuca adds its first-boot provisioning after writing. Needs a Pi with 4 GB of memory or more; smaller boards are refused at first boot with an explanation.
